_note: Regions (groups of inscriptions) and find sites. Coordinates are WGS 84 decimal degrees with an uncertainty radius in kilometres; they place the nearest settlement a source names, never the stone itself. A site with null coordinates is drawn only as part of its region's area. 'sources' are ids in sources.json.

area.basis: Talas town, with the valley around it

regions.summary: River boulders with epitaphs, most of them from Ayrtam-Ay near Talas town, and rock inscriptions in the gorges of the Talas Ala-Too (Kuru-Bakayir, Kenkol). Studied since 1896.

area.basis: Kochkor village, with the valley around it

regions.summary: Rock and boulder inscriptions found from 1998 by K. Tabaldiev and his colleagues, in the south-east of the valley (Kök-Say, Böyrök-Bulak).
The Chiyin-Tash rock inscriptions south of Ak-Ölön, near the western shore of the lake, and a stone statue from Taldy-Suu.
A rune-like inscription on the rim of a khum found in Sargata village.

sites.basis: Talas I was found 8 versts (about 8.5 km) from Talas town; plotted at the town.
sites.summary: A locality in the foothills of the Talas Ala-Too near Talas, with a kurgan cemetery partly destroyed when the 10th-century Karakhanid fort Keskentöbö was built. Twelve inscribed boulders and two stone statues are reported from it.
Where two stones are reported: the fourth Talas stone, on the southern outskirts, and a stone found by V. D. Serdyukov on a dairy farm on the western outskirts.
The gorge of the Kuru-Bakayir, a tributary of the Suuluu-Bakayir, in the Talas Ala-Too in the west of the Talas valley; petroglyphs, runic and Sogdian inscriptions.
The valley of the Kenkol, a tributary of the Talas, in the upper Talas valley; rock inscriptions, petroglyphs and tamgas.
Boulders in the south-eastern part of the Kochkor valley; the source names the mountain chain at whose foot they lie as Ukok.
East of Kök-Say, in the Kök-Say area.

sites.basis: Ak-Ölön village (Akulen), 42°20′24″N 76°09′36″E; the gorge is south of the village.
sites.summary: A gorge south of Ak-Ölön in Ton district, near the western shore of Issyk-Kul, on the way to Kök-Say. Locals call the spot the 'pictorial stone' for its many petroglyphs.
A village of Toktogul district; the khum was found on the ruins of a medieval fortress.
